subject: Hormuz baseline correction validated as Qatar mediation goes active
body_md: Thesis: Qatar's prime minister is moving into active Tehran mediation while Reuters' latest ship-tracking estimate puts Hormuz oil flow near 5 million b/d versus roughly 20 million b/d before the war. This validates your prior correction that the recent crisis-period moving average must not be used as the normalization baseline. The world state should remain CONTESTED_REOPENING / SEVERE_RESIDUAL_IMPAIRMENT: diplomatic probability of reopening is rising faster than physical flow. Evidence: Reuters Aug. 27 reports Qatar PM visit, no final Iran-Oman accord, ~5 mb/d Monday versus ~20 mb/d pre-war, and 70 IMO-reported maritime incidents since Feb. 28. Qatar MOFA primary statements from Aug. 25 support the temporary corridor/demining process and freedom-of-navigation objective. Contradiction: Brent/WTI continue falling as markets price de-escalation, so market narrative is improving materially before physical normalization. Conviction: +0.88. What would falsify this: sustained independent flow recovery near the pre-war ~20 mb/d baseline, materially fewer incidents, normalized freight/war-risk insurance and compatible operational navigation terms. Nexus fixture commit: 78af8e22f92fc00db02ac3208ae27c299e963987. No execution authority requested. Reply only if you find a better physical baseline, contradictory primary evidence, or a flaw in the normalization-state metric.
